messages.subject: Error while using DArT data for recombination analysis
messages.subject_clean: Error while using DArT data for recombination analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I want to use Poppr for analysis of DArT (dominant markers)data for haploid fungal pathogens to study frequency and diversity of pathogen in the field. This is how my data look like and it is stored in CSV format. The total number of individuals are 200 and markers are 6000 and above.

 content of filename.csv

Marker00001 Marker00002 Marker00003
1 1 1 1
2 1 01
3 01 1
4 1 1 NA

I converted the CSV file into genind and genind2pop using adegenet package
R script:
file <- read.csv(file="filename.csv", head=TRUE, sep=",")
obj <- df2genind(file, ploidy=1, type="PA")
obj2 <- genind2genpop(obj)
package(poppr)
data("obj2")
   Warning message:
    In data("obj2") : data set ‘obj2’ not found

I tried to use it as data("obj2") as well as for "obj" variable in poppr with and without "" but doesn't seem to work.

I am pretty sure, I am not doing it right but couldn't figure out what is happening. If someone can help me with this, I would be very grateful.

Many Thanks.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Barsha,

See my comments below.

> file <- read.csv(file="filename.csv", head=TRUE, sep=",")
> obj <- df2genind(file, ploidy=1, type="PA")
> obj2 <- genind2genpop(obj)
> package(poppr)

Everything above seems correct except for "package(poppr)". What you want is "library(poppr)".

> data("obj2")
>    Warning message:
>     In data("obj2") : data set ‘obj2’ not found
>
> I tried to use it as data("obj2") as well as for "obj" variable in poppr with and without "" but doesn't seem to work.

You don't need to use "data()". If you type "obj" or "obj2" in your R console (without quotes), you'll find a genind/genpop object printed to your screen.

The "data()" function is meant to load pre-existing dataset within a package.

I hope that helps,

Zhian

messages.subject: Re: how to write genetic distance values between genotypes to csv file in mat using POPPr package in R ?
messages.subject_clean: how to write genetic distance values between genotypes to csv file in mat using POPPr package in R ?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Genetist,

There are two ways to get what you want, depending on what you want, exactly.

If you want a lower triangle distance matrix, you can use the sink() function like so:

snpsdist <- bitwise.dist(snps)
sink(file = "GPdist.txt") # open the file
snpsdist # print output to file
sink() # close the file

There is also another way posted here: http://r.789695.n4.nabble.com/Write-lower-half-of-distance-matrix-only-td863971.html

If what you really want is a symmetrical square matrix, then you should convert it to a matrix and use write.table:

snpsdist <- bitwise.dist(snps)
write.table(as.matrix(snpsdist), file = "GPdist.csv", rownames = TRUE, colnames = NA, sep = ",")

The reason why your previous approach didn't work is because the save() function is a bit misleading as it saves data in a way R can understand, but not in a way that is useful outside of R.

Hope that helps!
Zhian
